title: Los vecinos
desc: You have neighbours whether you want them or not

sn.s: El patio de doña Carmen no tiene pared.
sn.e: Doña Carmen's patio has no wall.

sn.s: El patio sigue hasta el patio del vecino.
sn.e: The patio runs on into the neighbour's patio.

sn.s: Y ese patio sigue hasta el otro.
sn.e: And that patio runs on into the next.

sn.s: Los chavalos pasan de un patio a otro.
sn.e: The kids move from one patio to another.
The dogs do too.

sn.s: Todo el mundo entra al patio de todo el mundo.
sn.e: Everybody comes into everybody's patio.

sn.s: El primer día una señora entra al patio.
sn.e: On the first day a woman comes into the patio.
She does not knock.
"Buenas," she says. "Are you the new one?"
"Yes," I answer.
And the questions start.
"What is your name?"
I answer my name.
"And how old are you?"
I answer my age.
"And what do you do for work?"
I answer about my work.
"And are you married or single?"
That question surprises me.
"Single," I answer.
"And where is your family?"
"Far away," I say.
"Oh, poor thing!" the woman says.

sn.s: En cuatro minutos ya sabe todo.
sn.e: In four minutes she knows everything.

sn.s: Mi nombre, mi edad, mi trabajo.
sn.e: My name, my age, my job.
Whether I am married or single.
And where my family is.

sn.s: En mi país eso sería raro.
sn.e: In my country that would be strange.
You do not ask somebody's age.

sn.s: Uno no pregunta si es casado.
sn.e: You do not ask if they are married.
I say that to Roberto.

sn.s: "¿Y entonces cómo se conocen?", pregunta él.
sn.e: "So how do people get to know each other?" he asks.
I do not know what to answer.

sn.s: Aquí la pregunta no es mala educación.
sn.e: Here the question is not bad manners.
Here the question is interest.
Not asking would be the strange thing.

sn.s: Sería como decir que no le importa.
sn.e: It would be like saying you do not care.

sn.s: Después de una semana yo también pregunto.
sn.e: After a week I ask too.

sn.s: Le pregunto la edad a un vecino.
sn.e: I ask a neighbour his age.
I ask about his family.
I ask what work he does.
The neighbour answers everything, happily.
He is called don Beto.
Don Beto is sixty.
Don Beto works fixing bicycles.

sn.s: Don Beto es casado y tiene cinco hijos.
sn.e: Don Beto is married and has five children.

sn.s: Tres hijos viven en Costa Rica.
sn.e: Three of his children live in Costa Rica.
That he says more slowly.

sn.s: En el patio siempre hay alguien.
sn.e: There is always somebody in the patio.

sn.s: En el patio nadie está solo.
sn.e: Nobody is alone in the patio.
At first I wanted to be alone.

sn.s: Ahora no me acuerdo por qué.
sn.e: Now I cannot remember why.
